### The role

We are seeking a Critical Infrastructure Engineer to help ensure the availability, resilience, and operational readiness of the critical systems supporting Nebius data center IT infrastructure.

The primary objective of this role is uptime.

You will provide technical oversight across the electrical and mechanical infrastructure responsible for delivering reliable power and cooling to our GPU and IT environments. Rather than serving primarily as a maintenance technician, you will verify that critical infrastructure is operated safely, consistently, and in accordance with established SLAs, engineering standards, change-control procedures, and operational best practices.

You will also act as an important bridge between IT infrastructure teams and electrical/mechanical specialists. The ideal candidate understands how servers, networking equipment, racks, and GPU systems operate inside a data center while also having enough exposure to critical facilities systems to understand—and challenge when necessary—the infrastructure supporting them.

The position combines technical analysis, provider governance, change management, incident response, and hands-on familiarity with data center IT environments.

You will work onsite in our Minnesota data center location.

## Your responsibilities will include:

### Critical Infrastructure & Uptime

- Help ensure the availability and operational readiness of the electrical and mechanical infrastructure supporting production data halls and high-density GPU environments.

- Monitor critical infrastructure performance against contractual SLAs, operational requirements, and established reliability standards.

- Develop a strong understanding of the complete power and cooling path supporting IT equipment and identify conditions that could introduce operational risk.

- Review infrastructure capacity, redundancy, and operating conditions to ensure the environment can reliably support current and planned compute deployments.

- Identify infrastructure risks and work with service providers and internal teams to drive corrective actions before they impact production.

- Support infrastructure planning for data center expansions, capacity increases, and new GPU deployments.

### Power & Electrical Infrastructure

- Provide technical oversight of data center electrical infrastructure, including generator plants, automatic transfer switches (ATS), UPS systems, battery banks, switchgear, breakers, busbars, bus plugs, PDUs, and related power distribution equipment.

- Understand electrical distribution from facility-level infrastructure through rack-level delivery and IT equipment.

- Participate in technical reviews involving power capacity, electrical distribution, equipment sizing, redundancy, and infrastructure design.

- Work with electrical engineers and infrastructure providers to evaluate proposed changes and ensure appropriate engineering validation is completed before production implementation.

### Cooling & Mechanical Infrastructure

- Understand the cooling architecture supporting high-density GPU and IT environments, including water and glycol loops, rear-door heat exchangers (RDHx), evaporative systems, coolant distribution systems, facility water systems, dry coolers, and chillers.

- Evaluate how cooling infrastructure interacts with GPU systems and high-density racks to maintain required operating conditions.

- Partner with mechanical engineers and service providers to review system performance, capacity constraints, and proposed infrastructure changes.

- Identify potential thermal or cooling risks that could affect compute availability or future capacity.

### Provider Governance & Change Control

- Provide technical oversight of third-party critical infrastructure and colocation service providers.

- Ensure provider activities comply with Nebius policies, approved procedures, contractual SLAs, and operational requirements.

- Review and approve change requests involving critical infrastructure supporting production environments.

- Challenge incomplete or high-risk work plans and ensure appropriate testing, rollback procedures, risk analysis, and stakeholder communication are in place before work begins.

- Maintain strong governance around maintenance and infrastructure changes that could affect production availability.

- Hold service providers accountable for corrective actions, operational performance, and agreed service levels.

### Incident Response & Operational Risk

- Participate in critical infrastructure incidents and coordinate technical response with providers, Data Center IT, networking, and engineering teams.

- Support root-cause analysis following power, cooling, or infrastructure-related incidents.

- Review incident findings and ensure corrective and preventive actions are documented, assigned, and completed.

- Help develop and continuously improve emergency response procedures, escalation paths, change-control standards, and operational documentation.

- Identify recurring infrastructure risks and drive improvements that increase reliability and reduce the likelihood of customer impact.

### IT & Critical Infrastructure Integration

- Work closely with Data Center IT teams to understand how critical infrastructure conditions affect servers, networking equipment, GPU clusters, and other production systems.

- Apply practical knowledge of data center IT operations, including racks, servers, fiber, cabling, network equipment, and hardware deployment.

- Support cross-functional troubleshooting where the root cause may span IT equipment and facility infrastructure.

- Help create stronger operational alignment between IT infrastructure and electrical/mechanical teams.

### Reporting & Stakeholder Communication

- Translate complex infrastructure conditions, incidents, risks, and provider performance into clear information for technical and business leadership.

- Develop reports, dashboards, presentations, and operational analyses related to uptime, infrastructure performance, capacity, incidents, and service-provider performance.

- Participate in technical and leadership meetings as a subject-matter resource for data center critical infrastructure.

- Use operational data to identify trends, communicate risk, and drive measurable improvements in reliability and provider performance.

## We expect you to have:

- Experience working in data center, cloud infrastructure, colocation, critical facilities, or other mission-critical environments.

- Practical understanding of IT infrastructure, including servers, racks, networking equipment, structured cabling, and fiber.

- Working knowledge of data center electrical infrastructure such as UPS systems, generators, switchgear, PDUs, batteries, breakers, and power distribution.

- Exposure to data center mechanical and cooling systems, including chilled-water, glycol, liquid-cooling, or comparable thermal-management environments.

- Ability to understand how electrical and mechanical infrastructure directly impacts IT equipment availability and performance.

- Experience participating in infrastructure change management, incident response, operational risk management, or maintenance governance.

- Ability to review technical plans, ask detailed engineering questions, identify risk, and work effectively with electrical and mechanical subject-matter experts.

- Strong analytical skills with experience using Excel for reporting, data analysis, and operational metrics.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively with engineers, vendors, service providers, and senior leadership.

- A proactive, ownership-driven approach with the ability to operate effectively in a high-availability production environment.

## Nice to have:

- Experience supporting high-density GPU, AI, HPC, or hyperscale data center environments.

- Experience with direct-to-chip liquid cooling or other advanced cooling technologies used for high-density compute.

- Experience managing colocation or third-party critical infrastructure providers against contractual SLAs.

- Familiarity with Tier III data center environments and high-availability infrastructure principles.

- Experience developing or implementing change-management, incident-response, or emergency-response procedures.

Duration: 3 months
Start date: January 2027
Compensation: Paid
Eligibility: Current University student (Computer Science or related field), Recent Graduate or Early Career specialist 
Work authorization: Permitted to work in the job's location

Program Overview 

The Nebius IT Data Center Technician Early Talent program is a structured 3-month work experience designed to introduce early-career candidates to hands-on enterprise data center operations. Early talent participants are embedded on the data center floor as active team members alongside experienced DC Technicians and senior operations staff. Over the program, participants develop foundational technical skills, learn Nebius operational standards and safety procedures, and progress from fully supervised tasks toward working with increasing independence as their competency is demonstrated and validated. 

What You Will Do 

As an IT Data Center Technician Early Talent participant, you will work on the data center floor under the direct guidance of an experienced DC Technician. All hands-on work begins under close supervision. As you demonstrate proficiency and adherence to Nebius safety and operational standards, you will progressively take on tasks with greater independence — working toward completing assigned activities with minimal supervision by end of program. 

Hardware & Infrastructure 

- Learn to identify, handle, and document server components, rack hardware, and data center equipment under direct technician supervision.

- Observe and assist with physical installation, cabling, and labeling of server hardware in rack enclosures under guidance.

- Assist with hardware inventory counts, asset tagging, and equipment tracking tasks as directed.

- Shadow and support technicians during component replacements, hardware decommissions, and equipment staging activities.

- Begin performing basic rack and stack tasks independently once foundational procedures have been trained and validated.

Cabling & Connectivity 

- Learn copper and fiber cabling standards, patch cord management, and labeling practices used at Nebius data center sites.

- Assist with cable organization, dressing, and documentation under direct technician guidance.

- Support connectivity checks and basic cable tracing tasks as assigned.

Documentation & Ticketing 

- Learn to use Nebius ticketing and asset management systems for logging work, updating hardware records, and tracking assigned tasks.

- Assist with documentation of equipment configurations, cable layouts, and maintenance activities under technician review.

- Begin entering and updating tickets independently for assigned work items once system proficiency is demonstrated.

Safety & Operational Standards 

- Complete all required Nebius data center safety training, site access procedures, and equipment handling certifications at program start.

- Follow all safety protocols, access controls, and site procedures at all times while on the data center floor.

- Never work unsupervised on live infrastructure or perform any task outside your validated scope without direct technician authorization.

- Observe and learn Nebius operational standards including shift handoff procedures, escalation practices, and incident documentation. 

Learning & Development 

- Participate in structured weekly check-ins with your assigned DC Technician mentor to review skill progression and address questions.

- Complete assigned Nebius training modules covering hardware fundamentals, data center operations, and safety throughout the program.

- Shadow senior technicians during escalated incidents, complex deployments, and hardware troubleshooting activities to build technical awareness.

-  Actively engage during shadowing activities and take initiative in building your technical knowledge base throughout the 3 months.

Supervision & Progression 

Early talent participants begin under close, continuous supervision for all data center floor activities. This is not a desk-based or observation-only role — you are an active participant on the floor from day one. Progression follows a structured competency model: 

- Weeks 1–3: Orientation and shadowing. All tasks under direct supervision with step-by-step guidance. Focus on safety, site familiarity, system access, and equipment identification.

- Weeks 4–7: Assisted execution. You perform assigned tasks with your mentor present and reviewing all completed work before sign-off.

- Weeks 8–10: Supervised independence. You complete defined tasks independently within your validated scope, checking in at key milestones. Technician remains nearby and available.

- Weeks 11–12: Demonstrated competency. Qualified participants work with minimal supervision on fully validated tasks; technician oversight maintained for any task outside established scope.

Progression is based on demonstrated proficiency and adherence to Nebius standards — not time served. Participants who complete the program with strong evaluations will be considered for the Nebius early talent pipeline.

- Ability to stand and remain on your feet for extended periods during active floor operations.

- Ability to safely lift and position equipment up to 50 pounds unassisted; heavier loads with team-lift support.

- Comfortable working at heights including ladders, raised platforms, and elevated data center infrastructure.

- Ability to work in confined spaces such as under raised floors, within rack enclosures, and in cable management pathways.

- Comfortable in environments with variable temperatures including cold aisle containment zones.

- Manual dexterity to handle small form-factor components, precision cabling, and fine connector installations.

You will work on-site at our Alabama data center location.

- Own the daily operational performance of DC Technician and DC Facilities Engineering staff. Assign shift coverage, set priorities, balance workloads, and ensure open work is tracked, delegated, and completed to Nebius standards.

- Conduct regular one-on-one meetings with direct reports. Deliver structured performance feedback, set individual development goals aligned with the career framework, track progression, and manage performance concerns in partnership with HR and the Data Center IT Manager.

Nebius is building the AI infrastructure that financial institutions will run AI on in production, from quantitative research and real-time risk to agentic workflows in banks and insurers.

The Field CTO for Financial Services is a senior technical leadership role at the intersection of production GPU infrastructure and the regulated business of financial services. You will lead the technical side of the vertical: the architecture conversation with CTOs and heads of research infrastructure, the technical content of regulated-buyer diligence, the reference architectures for financial workloads, and the product requirements that come out of the field.

Financial institutions buy AI infrastructure differently from most customers. Quantitative funds and AI-native fintechs buy GPU capacity directly and judge it on price-performance, availability, and how the cluster behaves under their own workloads. Banks and insurers add a second review: security, third-party risk, data residency, and exit planning are assessed before a deal reaches architecture discussions. You will earn the trust of both kinds of buyer and help make Nebius an approved supplier to financial institutions.

You will work alongside the Head of Financial Services, Sales, Security and GRC, Product, and Engineering. The role begins as a hands-on individual contributor, with a clear path to building and leading forward deployed engineers as the vertical scales.

This is a ground-floor opportunity to define how financial institutions run AI in production on a specialized AI cloud.

You are welcome to work remotely from the United States (New York City preferred). Travel expectations are 10% to 20% for customer visits, executive meetings, and key industry events.

Your responsibilities will include:

- Executive Technical Leadership: Serve as the technical face of Nebius to financial services customers, partners, and ecosystem stakeholders. You will build and lead the organization responsible for deploying and operating Nebius AI infrastructure at our Independence, Missouri campus. Your team will bring together data center IT operations, critical facilities, networking, logistics, operational readiness, and supporting functions.

You will work closely with hardware, network, engineering, cloud, commercial, and corporate teams to bring compute capacity into service and establish reliable, scalable operations.

The role

We are seeking a General Manager, Data Center to lead the organizational build-out, hardware deployment, operational readiness, and ongoing performance of our gigawatt-scale data center campus in Independence, Missouri. This is an on-site leadership role with responsibility for the Independence campus.

You will have autonomy to design the campus organization, select your leadership team, define reporting lines, and establish the operating model within agreed budgets and company standards. You will own operational readiness and campus performance across critical facilities and IT infrastructure, aligning people, systems, and service partners to deliver reliable customer capacity.

The facility is currently under construction. You will partner with construction, engineering, and critical facilities teams to align facility completion, commissioning, and handover with hardware deployment and operational readiness. You will establish the operating team and coordinate GPU, server, network, and storage installation, integration, acceptance testing, and cloud readiness with the responsible technical teams and service providers.

This role offers the opportunity to shape the operating practices that support Nebius as its AI infrastructure business grows.

Your responsibilities will include:

Organization Design and Leadership

- Design and build the campus organization, including functional leadership, building and shift coverage, reporting lines, and clear decision authority.

- Hire, lead, and develop directors, data center managers, and operations teams in partnership with Talent Acquisition and HR.

- Own the phased workforce plan, aligning recruitment, training, contractor support, and leadership coverage with hardware deployment, acceptance testing, and production milestones.

- Establish performance expectations, consistent technical competency standards, and succession plans that support reliable campus operations and sustained performance.

Operational Deployment and Readiness

- Own the integrated operational readiness plan connecting facility completion and handover milestones, equipment delivery, hardware installation, network and storage integration, staffing, and customer service readiness.

- Coordinate with construction and facilities teams to verify power, cooling, and space readiness before deployment; manage dependencies and escalate gaps that could delay bringing capacity into service.

- Define operational acceptance criteria for the campus and deployed infrastructure, coordinate readiness and acceptance testing with technical owners, and accept or withhold operational handover against agreed requirements.

- Ensure trained teams, tested procedures, critical spares, asset records, monitoring, and vendor support are in place before production operations begin.

- Coordinate GPU, server, network fabric, storage, and cloud readiness with technical owners, and jointly confirm that released capacity can support customer workloads.

- Sequence hardware installation, integration, and production changes to protect live environments as additional compute capacity comes online.

Campus Operations and Reliability

- Own end-to-end campus operations across critical facilities and IT infrastructure, delivering agreed uptime, performance, and service levels.

- Establish 24/7 coverage, maintenance governance, change control, incident command, root-cause analysis, and business continuity practices.

- Ensure clear responsibility across power, liquid cooling, controls, hardware, networking, and cloud interfaces; hold owners accountable for corrective actions.

- Use monitoring, automation, and performance reporting to improve deployment throughput, repair turnaround, reliability, and operating efficiency.

- Own campus operating budgets, workforce costs, vendor expenditure, and forecasts within delegated authority; contribute to capital planning and investment priorities.

- Align power, cooling, rack space, equipment, and staffing capacity with deployment plans, and address constraints affecting customer commitments.

- Establish asset inventory, receiving, logistics, critical spares, repair, warranty-return, and secure disposition processes.

- Track budget variance, rework, delayed capacity, and operational losses; drive corrective actions and report financial impacts clearly.

Partners, City Coordination, Safety and Executive Accountability

- Coordinate with City of Independence departments alongside Public Affairs and Legal on site readiness, permitting and inspections, utility interfaces, emergency preparedness, and ongoing operational matters; align external communications and commitments with the responsible teams.

- Ensure safety, environmental, physical security, and applicable compliance requirements are implemented with the responsible specialists and corporate teams.

- Provide executive visibility into launch progress, workforce readiness, operating performance, financial forecasts, and risks requiring decisions.

Operational Scalability and Leadership Development

- Develop repeatable deployment standards, staffing models, acceptance practices, and operating procedures that support the campus as compute capacity scales.

The Role
We're looking for a Technical Leader for Network Infrastructure to own delivery of network infrastructure initiatives in the US. This is not a role for someone who only coordinates tickets and status. It is a role for someone with an engineering skeleton: a person who has built, operated, broken and recovered things, and can earn the trust of SREs, SWEs, network engineers, and security and platform teams. We are at the early stage of our US expansion, so at first you will be hands-on: reviewing designs, stepping into incidents, and writing code or automation when the team needs it, with a high degree of independence from the European teams. As the organization grows, the scope of the role will grow with it.

You own delivery. You will make important cross-team initiatives land: defining scope, aligning owners, exposing risks, driving decisions, tracking dependencies, and making sure we ship useful outcomes instead of half-finished initiatives. The job is not done when the technical pieces exist. It is done when engineers trust the tool, the NOC actually uses the workflow, alerts are actionable, runbooks are real, and the new way becomes the default way.

You stay technical. You don't need to be the deepest expert in every area, but you should be technical enough to understand real trade-offs: why rollback is not optional, why "just automate it" can create a bigger blast radius, why SLOs without ownership are decoration, and why network device CI/CD is very different from deploying a stateless service. You can read a design doc, challenge missing assumptions, notice unclear failure modes, and help the team turn a vague but important problem into an executable plan.

This is a high-leverage role in an early-stage and fast-scaling network infrastructure organisation. Many important systems are being built now: automation, observability, reliability standards, provisioning flows, operational safety, and cross-site consistency. You won't be maintaining a mature machine from the sidelines. You'll help shape how the machine works.

Your responsibilities will include:

- Set the engineering bar: code quality, design review, on-call and incident management practices, and operational standards

- Own end-to-end delivery of cross-team network infrastructure initiatives in the US, from a vague problem statement to an executable plan to adoption

- Define scope and success criteria, align owners across SRE, SWE, network, security, platform and data center teams, and drive decisions to closure

- Review designs and technical proposals, challenge missing assumptions, and surface failure modes, dependencies and risks early

- Stay hands-on where it matters: step into incidents, write code or automation, and unblock the team

- Drive adoption: make sure tools and workflows become the default way of working, with real documentation, runbooks and feedback loops

- Keep stakeholders, including the European teams, informed with clear, honest status and coordinate across time zones

- Turn operational pain and engineering input into a clear, prioritized backlog

We expect you to have:

- 7+ years of experience in software, SRE, network or infrastructure engineering, including experience leading cross-team technical initiatives

- A real engineering background: you have built and operated production systems and can earn the trust of deeply technical teams

- Ability to read design docs and technical proposals, understand trade-offs, and ask sharp questions about reliability, rollback, blast radius and failure modes

- Strong understanding of infrastructure fundamentals (Linux, networking, automation, CI/CD) at the level needed to hold your own in technical discussions

- Proven ability to drive decisions and create clarity in ambiguous, fast-changing environments

- Excellent written and verbal communication, including documenting plans and decisions and influencing smart technical people

- Experience with CI/CD or change management for network or other high-blast-radius infrastructure

- Experience building a team from scratch or launching a new engineering hub

- An SLO framework for network services and components, including SLIs, SLOs, dashboards, alerts, ownership, tiering, and a clear link between reliability targets and engineering investment
